name: Work on What Has Been Spoiled
momentumNotes: The movement turns toward repair; what was neglected can improve through deliberate work.
theme: What has been spoiled can become the beginning of repair. Decay is not only an ending; it is a message from what has been untended.
basicInterpretation: Look honestly at the old pattern, inherited habit, or neglected place. Patient correction can turn shame into stewardship.
reflectionPrompt: What asks to be repaired rather than hidden?

reversed.theme: Flipped upside down, Work on What Has Been Spoiled becomes Hexagram 17, Following. This other side brings in the atmosphere of adaptation, trust, response, asking how the situation may look from another threshold.
reversed.reflection: Let Following widen the reading rather than replace it. Consider what another person, timing, or hidden part of you might see when the pattern is viewed from the far side.
reversed.applicationPrompt: Visualize your question from the far side, as if another person or your future self is looking back through Following. Notice where adaptation, trust, response and a moving, adaptive movement reveal needs, timing, or motives that the first view may miss.

opposite.theme: The contrast to Work on What Has Been Spoiled is Hexagram 17, Following. Where the primary pattern emphasizes repair, neglect, inheritance, this complementary field points toward adaptation, trust, response.
opposite.reflection: In this reading, the complementary view is the same hexagram as the Other Side. This suggests that what the situation is not, and how it may appear from another angle, are part of the same teaching.
opposite.applicationPrompt: Visualize Following as the contrasting color laid beside Work on What Has Been Spoiled. Ask what hidden cause, missing medicine, or opposing pressure is suggested by adaptation, trust, response, especially where the situation carries a supportive, adaptive tone.
